title: Safe Quantum Stochastic Linear Bandits
claim: Several interaction models differ in whether actions and feedback are classical or coherent, and the last adds a safety-flag bomb.
layout: 3 panels, two on top and one below, circuit diagrams
description: Three quantum-circuit diagrams on a white background, drawn in black line art. Panel (a), top left, shows a box labeled O_a. Input wires labeled |0> enter from the left. Output wires |ω> and |X(a,ω)> leave on the right, grouped by a bracket into |χ_a>. Panel (b), top right, shows a box labeled E_a with |0> inputs. Its outputs go to two meter (measurement) icons, followed by the text X ~ D_a. Panel (c), bottom center, shows a box labeled O with three inputs: |a>, |0>_flag and |0>. The outputs are |a>, a meter on the flag wire with a double line leading to '1 ⇒ explode', and |χ_a>. Captions under each panel name the model: classical-action coherent-feedback, classical-action classical-feedback, and coherent-action coherent-feedback with a safe-action bomb. The eye goes first to the boxes, then to the meters.
caption: Safe quantum bandit models. In [ref], each action $a$ has a corresponding unitary oracle $\mathcal{O}_a$ that prepares a coherent qsample of the stochastic feedback. In [ref], each query applies a quantum channel $\mathcal{E}_a$ followed by measurement, yielding classical feedback. In [ref], the learner queries actions in superposition (first register) while the oracle attaches a safety flag (second register) and prepares the reward qsample (third register); measuring $1$ on the flag register triggers a bomb explosion and terminates the algorithm.
abstract: We initiate the study of safe quantum stochastic linear bandits, in which a learner maximizes an unknown linear reward while satisfying unknown linear mean constraints at every interaction. Under coherent unitary access to the joint reward-and-constraint distribution, we develop QRS-COLTS, a staged quantum resampled-scaling analog of constrained linear Thompson sampling (COLTS). With high probability, QRS-COLTS plays only feasible actions and achieves regret that is polylogarithmic in the query horizon and scales only with the square root of the number of constraints. We also study a model in which the learner queries superpositions of actions while an unsafe-action flag, a "bomb" that terminates the interaction upon violation, is measured after every query. In this setting, the bomb provides exact membership access to the safe set, and query regret is evaluated over the action superposition. For this model, we propose BCO-QLinTS, which selects feasible actions via bomb-certified quantum convex optimization without estimating the constraint matrix. Its query-weighted regret remains polylogarithmic in the horizon, with the constraints entering the bound only through the geometry of the safe set.
